hook.en: Many languages in the world today are spoken by fewer and fewer people. The Last Lesson asks what we lose when a language is taken from us.

objectives.en: Identify the main themes of the story
Explain linguistic chauvinism and the love of one's mother tongue
Recognise irony, symbolism and pathos in the story

narration.en: Many languages in the world today are spoken by fewer and fewer people. The Last Lesson asks what we lose when a language is taken from us.

body.en: The central theme is the pain of losing one's language, which is closely tied to identity and freedom. Linguistic chauvinism means forcing one's own language on others and treating it as superior; here the conquerors impose German. Another theme is procrastination: Franz, the parents and even M. Hamel kept putting off learning, and now it is too late.

points.en: Love of the mother tongue and identity
Patriotism and the dignity of the conquered

say.en: At the centre is language, which carries a people's identity.
The conquerors force their own language on others. That is linguistic chauvinism.
M. Hamel links holding on to one's language with keeping freedom alive.
Everyone kept putting off learning. Now there is no tomorrow.
The farewell message shows deep love for France.
Franz and the villagers regret the time they wasted.
The irony: Franz values French only on the day he loses it.

body.en: Daudet uses irony: Franz begins to love French on the very day he loses the chance to learn it. Symbols carry the emotion: the bulletin board stands for bad news, the pigeons cooing on the roof make Franz wonder whether even they will be made to sing in German, and the copybooks look like little flags. The ending, where M. Hamel cannot speak, is full of pathos.

points.en: Irony: interest awakens only when it is too late
Symbols: bulletin board, pigeons, copybooks like flags
Contrast: the noisy usual school versus the silent last day

problem.en: What does the story teach us about our attitude to our own language and to learning?

steps.en: State the lesson: value your mother tongue; it is part of who you are.
Add the warning against procrastination: opportunities may not return.
Link to today: respect every language; do not impose one on others.

answer.en: The story teaches us to cherish our mother tongue as part of our identity and not to take learning for granted, because, like Franz, we may realise its worth only when it is lost. We should also respect other people's languages.
